question: 400 custard apples were bought at ₹1200 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹900. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of custard apples.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of 1 apple = 1200 ÷ 100 = ₹12

Profit per apple = 900 ÷ 400 = ₹2.25

Selling Price (SP) of 1 apple = 12 + 2.25 = ₹14.25

SP of 1 dozen (12 apples) = 14.25 × 12 = ₹171

**∴ The correct answer is ₹171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total custard apples bought = 400

Cost Price (CP) per 100 apples = ₹1200

Total Profit on selling 400 apples = ₹900

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) + Profit

Value per dozen = (Total Value ÷ Total Quantity) × 12

 Calculation for 400 Custard Apples
 
 
 Total CP = ₹4800
 
 
 Profit = ₹900
 
 

 
 Total SP = ₹4800 + ₹900 = ₹5700
 SP per dozen = (₹5700 ÷ 400) × 12 = ₹171

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP for 400 apples = (1200 ÷ 100) × 400 = ₹4800

⇒ Total SP for 400 apples = CP + Profit = 4800 + 900 = ₹5700

⇒ SP for 12 apples (1 dozen) = (Total SP × 12) ÷ Total apples

⇒ SP per dozen = (5700 × 12) ÷ 400

⇒ SP per dozen = 57 × (12 ÷ 4) = 57 × 3

⇒ SP per dozen = ₹171

**∴ The correct answer is ₹171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit and loss are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is offered on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the effective single discount percentage is equal to (a + b − a × b ÷ 100)%.
